httpStatus is guarded with a truthiness check (context.httpStatus && …) instead of an explicit undefined check, mirroring the same inconsistency found in the mixpanel error-tracking mapper.

The dedupe key is computed by hashing only the emitted properties from the hand-maintained mapContext whitelist, not the full ErrorContext, so the PR description's claim that a newly added facet cannot be forgotten only holds if that new field is also wired into mapContext; this invariant is undocumented and unenforced.

Dedupe correctness relies on JSON.stringify iterating object properties in a stable insertion order; if mapContext is later refactored to conditionally build keys in a different order (e.g. via Object.fromEntries with filtering), logically identical events could produce different serialized keys and stop being deduplicated.

pruneSentErrors scans the whole map twice on overflow (once for expired entries, once for LRU eviction), which is an unnecessary O(n) pass that could be addressed with Map#entries() slicing if the tracked-error ceiling grows.

Test coverage does not verify that the suppressed occurrence counter resets to 0 when the same error key resurfaces after the dedupe window; there is no test asserting that a re-emit following the window, followed immediately by another failure, reports 1 occurrence rather than continuing from the prior count (e.g. 4).
